newsitem.title: USA: Car links Chicago mogul's slaying to Minn. deaths.
newsitem.headline: Car links Chicago mogul's slaying to Minn. deaths.

text.p: Authorities prepared murder charges Wednesday against a man suspected of a twin killing in the Minneapolis area who may also be linked to the weekend slaying of a Chicago real estate mogul, officials said.
Police were searching for Andrew Cunanan, 27, a San Diego native, and the missing black-green Lexus automobile belonging to slain Chicago tycoon Lee Miglin, 72.

Chisago County, Minnesota, prosecutor James Ruder said Cunanan would be charged with two murder counts in the deaths last week of Minneapolis architect David Madson and his alleged lover Jeffrey Trail.
Officials said Madson was shot to death, apparently after witnessing Trail being bludgeoned, allegedly by Cunanan in what may have been a fit of jealousy.

The possible link to Miglin's weekend slaying was a Jeep Grand Cherokee believed to be Madson's. The vehicle was parked illegally for the past few days near Miglin's garage where his body was found bound with tape, his throat cut by a saw.
Chicago police said they had seized the vehicle and were combing it for fingerprints and other clues.

Miglin was chairman of Miglin-Beitler Inc., a real estate development company. A decade ago the company announced plans to build a 125-floor office tower in downtown Chicago that at the time would have been the world's tallest such structure. Plans for the building were later abandoned.
